correctness.rationale: Every binary idempotent satisfies (M^T-I)x=0; any perfect matrix is invertible. Subspace Möbius inversion with interval value (-1)^j2^{j choose 2}, exact fixed-U count 2^{r(n-r)}GL(n-r), gives all-rank formula. Irreducible companions prove n≥2 nonzero-idempotent-free examples, n1 is impossible. Perfect-natural-basis uniqueness restricts isomorphisms to permutations over F2; direct exhaustive orbit partition through n4 with independent permutation conjugation and exact stabilizer sizes gives 1,8,248. Stdlib code executed and returned VERIFY_OK, with 248 orbit sizes 8×2+12×8+24×238=5824.

value.rationale: A natural field-sensitive distinction: the 2025 complete-evolution work guarantees a nonzero idempotent in its complex setting, whereas over F2 perfect algebras can have none from the sharp minimum dimension two. The all-rank probability distribution of every possible idempotent count, and precise 248 four-dimensional isomorphism classes meeting the obstruction, are natural classification invariants; unlike an arbitrary matrix count they directly distinguish an algebraically motivated idempotent-property stratum.
